title: Bidirectional Dijkstra in Valencia: Faster Routes!
description: See how Bidirectional Dijkstra finds the shortest path across Valencia’s old-city street grid by searching forward and backward at the same time. Watch the frontier meet and shrink the explored area compared to classic single-source search.
ig_caption:
🧠⚡ Bidirectional Dijkstra in Valencia (Ciutat Vella)! 🌍🚦

Instead of running one Dijkstra from the start until it reaches the goal, Bidirectional Dijkstra launches two coordinated searches on the same weighted graph: one forward from the source and one backward from the destination. 🧩➡️⬅️ As the priority queues expand, the algorithm stops when the best possible connection (via settled/expanded nodes) can’t improve the current shortest path estimate.

📌 Graph theory lens: your street map becomes a weighted graph G(V, E) where intersections are vertices and road segments are edges with costs (distance, travel time, or penalties). By meeting in the middle, we drastically reduce the explored region—especially on large, dense road networks.

🎥 Watch the visualization: nodes light up from both directions until the fronts collide and the optimal route is stitched together.

👉 Want a version that uses turn costs or one-way streets? Comment your rules and hit follow for more real-map algorithm reels! ✅
fb_caption:
Valencia’s old streets turned into a weighted graph—and Bidirectional Dijkstra does the work fast! 🗺️⚙️

This visualization shows how two simultaneous Dijkstra searches (from start and goal) meet in the middle, reducing the number of expanded nodes while still guaranteeing the shortest path on positive weights. If you learn better by watching, share this with a friend who likes graph search and drop a comment: should we add one-way streets next?
